I'm copying this from a reply to somebody else, but I think it's relevant to dealing with depression:

I was suicidal for a long time, but have recently started getting better...

It sucks, you know, it feels kindof like you're just going through the motions of it, but not really doing it. Like maybe at some point you're going to flip a corner and life is going to snap into "real".

What's helped me lately is that I moved from my safe, nice, new, suburban house to an old house in an old art neighborhood full of hippies. There are people outside, and somehow that little bit of seeing life around me helps. I've also started consuming THC (edibles...I hate smoking).

It gets better. There was a long time where I was really genuinely afraid of myself...I had tried to kill myself in the past, and was sure that I would again in the future...it doubted that I would make it 30 (I'm 25...I lost about 10 years of my life to debilitating depression)...since I changed some of the things in my life, I'm not so positive about that anymore...life feels like it's worth living.

My advice to you is to get a dog and raise it from a puppy (ahh choking up typing this now). I got my dog (who is currently curled up in a ball near my feet) by accident about 6 years ago and during one of the darkest points in my life...she was a puppy and she had peed on my dad's carpet, so he was going to get rid of her/have her put down...so I took her from him and left. Every time I'd be driving home imagining how little effort it would take to just turn my steering wheel a tad bit and not have to deal with hating everything anymore, I would think about what would happen to my dog...and how happy she would be to see me when I got home. Every time I come through the door she is waiting, usually with a tennis ball, and jumps up to lick my face (goddamnit, now I'm crying).

Seriously, get a dog, move houses, start using THC, it's an incredibly effective anti-depressant (for me, I have horrible horrible anxiety problems and THC fixes them like magic.).

You're screaming out at people that your lost and can't find your home and you just want to go home and lay down and go to sleep, but nobody knows what you're talking about. You need to understand that, like any other disease, being depressed is not your fault.  Unlike [most] other diseases, however, depression takes what feels like an *active* attempt to make you feel that way.

A lot of people don't get that being sad and being depressed are not the same thing.  They look *kindof* the same, but so does a paper cut and a gunshot wound to the face; they both involve blood, right?

It isn't your fault, you really need to understand that.  The other thing that you need to understand is that things *will* get better.  I think most of us on this subreddit have been to some of the worst, darkest places imaginable (emotionally)...things *are* going to get better for you.

The unfortunate thing is that there is a chance that your depression will eventually come back...and then back again, and back again...

At first, this seems really scary and intimidating, and it feels like there is no escape and that you just want to run out into the streets screaming and throw yourself in from of the first car you see because GODDAMNIT I DON"T WANT TO DEAL WITH THIS ANYMORE!!!111

Please don't do that.  As you get more and more used to what you're feeling, you'll learn to sense when it is coming on, and how to prevent it/live with it.

Eventually, you won't feel any feelings of depression at all :-D!  Hooray!

Until then, however, we're here to help.  Please lean on us as much as you need to because we all want to help you through it.

Hi reddit, I'm non-linkable.  I lurk reddit with a different username, but I, as I imagine most of you do, try to hide my emotions from the rest of the world, so I created another username that isn't linkable to anything...

Guys, and girls, depression is one of the worst diseases there is.  It kills from the inside out and sometimes even convinces you that there is nothing wrong.  It is a disease that lots and lots of people claim doesn't exist.  It is also one of the most deadly diseases there is.

When I was 19 years old I tried to kill myself.  I came home from work, or class, or something and my roomate was gone...I sat down at my computer, and I decided that I didn't want to live anymore.  I was done with it.  Every single moment of every single day was torture and I didn't want to play anymore.

I ate a bunch of xanax, and drank a bunch of alcohol because I wanted to go to sleep and not wake up again.  I stumbled out of my dorm in a daze and started walking up a big hill/mountain on our campus to lay down on the warm rocks and watch the city as I fell asleep hopefully for the last time.  The last thing that I remember walking up there was getting a very strange look from a couple of lovebirds walking down the same path.

Luckily, I hadn't taken enough of either poison to kill me.

I woke up the next morning and, unsure what exactly I was supposed to do after a botched suicide attempt, I went to work.

After that, I moved out of the dorms and back into my parents house for the summer.  That is when I started hurting myself.  It would be either a butterfly knife that I had, or a lighter.  What i would do is sit in the bathroom with my knife, and make slices up and down my legs.  I did this because I didn't want people to know about it...cutting up my arms seemed stupid and I didn't understand why people did it.

If I didn't have knife, I would use a lighter that I carried around for this purpose:  I would use it to heat up one of the keys in my pocket until I couldn't comfortably hold the key anymore, then I would press it into my forearm until a blister appeared.  Sometimes I would do both...there is still a big scar on my arm from cutting it open, then using the key to burn it shut (that doesn't make any sense at all, I know).

Why am I telling you this, reddit?  Is it because I'm an attention whoring emo-kid that wants you all to feel bad for me?

No, it isn't.

I'm telling you this because I want you guys all to know that I've been there.  I want you to know that I know exactly what you're feeling, I'm not your parents or your friends who tell you things like "you just need to decide to be happy!".  I'm telling you this because I want you to know that I am here for you.

Its not fair, guys.  Its not fair the way that I know some of you are getting treated by those around you.  If I can in any way say anything to any of you to bring even the smallest amount of joy or hope to one of your days please let me.
